objective: Learn representations capturing relationships between medical images and associated captions; fixed image and text features will support subsequent paired representation learning.

inspection.measurements: Official train: 59,958 complete pairs and unique IDs; official validation: 9,904 complete pairs and unique IDs. Among up to 1,000 sampled per split, training caption word median 18, p10 7, p90 39; validation median 18, p10 7, p90 42. Sampled empty captions: 0 train, 1 validation. Unique caption fraction 1.0 in each sample. These are inspection samples, not a guarantee for all captions.

configurations.name: selected
configurations.image: Frozen ImageNet-pretrained ResNet18 with its pretrained image transforms and 512-dimensional output; no additional image dimension reduction. Semantic-oriented features fit image-caption relationships better than color alone, though ImageNet features are not radiology-specific.
configurations.text: Training-fitted TF-IDF, English stop words, min_df=2, up to 12,000 unigram and bigram features, then training-fitted 128-component truncated SVD. Median 18-word captions can contain useful multiword terms; the vocabulary cap and SVD bound memory and output dimensionality for 8,000 training examples. Counts are pragmatic capacity choices, not benchmarked optima.
configurations.compute: Higher image inference cost on host MPS; sparse TF-IDF and SVD add CPU and memory cost.

configurations.name: lower-cost alternative
configurations.image: 96-dimensional RGB color histogram, resized to 128x128; no semantic image encoder.
configurations.text: Hashing with 12,000 bins, unigram-only features and 128-component training-fitted SVD; fixed feature space avoids vocabulary fitting but admits collisions and loses term interpretability.
configurations.compute: Cheaper CPU image extraction and smaller image features; loses spatial and semantic information relevant to medical image-caption relationships.

rejected_alternatives: Color histograms discard image structure and semantics, despite low cost.
Hashing avoids vocabulary storage but has collisions and reduced interpretability; the inspected corpus and requested 8,000 training rows support capped TF-IDF.
Unigram-only TF-IDF is cheaper but may miss multiword medical terms; bigrams are bounded by the feature cap. None of these alternatives was benchmarked.
split_and_leakage: Sample 9,000 distinct IDs from official training with seed 42, use first 8,000 for training and remaining 1,000 for validation; sample 1,000 from official validation for held-out test. Script drops missing captions and duplicate IDs and checks image paths. Vocabulary, IDF and SVD are fitted only on the 8,000 training captions; frozen transformations apply to both held-out splits. Image weights and preprocessing are fixed. Inspect prepared outputs and verify IDs, pairing, split disjointness and finite values before training.
resource_and_limitations: MPS and pretrained weights must be available to the host; weights may require download. Batch size 32 bounds inference memory. TF-IDF is sparse prior to SVD. The requested SVD dimension is capped by available training rows and vocabulary. One sampled official-validation caption was empty; missing captions are dropped by the script, so inspect the actual manifests and output for empty text. ResNet18 and text vectorizer are not fine-tuned; this is not end-to-end CLIP.
command: python analysis/prepare_dataset_1.py --source data/dataset_1 --output outputs/final_dataset_1/prepared --train-size 8000 --validation-size 1000 --eval-size 1000 --batch-size 32 --seed 42 --device mps --image-encoder resnet18 --text-vectorizer tfidf --text-max-features 12000 --text-components 128 --text-ngram-max 2
